title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Scheduling Operations Agent optimises multiple resources at once
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap and Microsoft Learn, including its controls, consumption billing and conditional automatic enablement. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's 30-resource batch limit from Learn's preview limit of 50; add the Field Service BookingStatus reference to support the writable column and option values.

claims.claim: This roadmap change expands the Field Service Scheduling Operations Agent to optimize multiple resources.
claims.quote: This release expands the optimization capabilities of the Scheduling Operations Agent to include multiple resources.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists optimization of up to five resources directly from the schedule board.
claims.quote: Optimize schedules for up to 5 resources directly from the schedule board.

claims.quote: Before dispatchers can use the agent, an administrator must set it up in your environment. ... You have an administrator role in Dynamics 365.

claims.claim: The Field Service toggle path is Resources > Scheduling Parameters > Resource Scheduling > Agents > Scheduling Operations Agent (Preview).
claims.quote: Open the Field Service app. ... Change to the Resources area and go to Scheduling Parameters > Resource Scheduling. ... Go to the Agents tab and turn on Scheduling Operations Agent (Preview).

claims.claim: No API is documented for the agent enablement toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: "Scheduling Operations Agent" "enable" "API"; site:learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365 "msdyn" "Scheduling Operations Agent" "enabled". Read soa-setup and scheduling-parameters-settings Agents excerpt; no toggle API found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The agent toggle enables interactive and batch optimizations together.
claims.quote: Turning on the agent enables both interactive and batch optimizations.

claims.claim: User roles are assigned through environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles > the named agent role in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select your environment, and then go to Settings > Users + permissions > Users. ... Select a user, and then select Manage security roles. ... Select Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator or Scheduling Operations Agent User

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment id> --user <user principal name> --role <role name> assigns the selected security role.
claims.quote: Assign a user to a target Dataverse environment with specified security role. ... --role: Name or ID of security role ... --user: Object ID or user principal name (UPN) ... --environment: ID or URL of the environment

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator role allows creating scopes, goals and plans.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator ... Create, edit, and delete scopes, goals, and plans, and view optimization results.

claims.where: controls[1].note; controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Scheduling Operations Agent User role allows interactive optimizations and running existing batch plans.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent User ... View scopes, goals, and plans; run interactive optimizations from the schedule board and batch optimizations from a plan; and view optimization results.

claims.claim: Agent roles are additive to a role granting access to underlying scheduling tables, such as Field Service - Dispatcher.
claims.quote: They're additive, so assign them alongside a user's existing roles rather than replacing them. Each user also needs a role that grants access to the underlying scheduling tables

claims.claim: User roles are assigned per environment.
claims.quote: Select your environment, and then go to Settings > Users + permissions > Users.

claims.claim: The agent runs as an application user in the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: The agent runs as an application user that belongs to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.

claims.claim: Changes use the combined permissions of the initiating user and application user, both of whom need record access.
claims.quote: Each change the agent makes uses the combined permissions of the user who runs the optimization and the agent's application user, so both must have access to the affected records.

claims.claim: The application user can read and write standard scheduling tables by default.
claims.quote: By default, the agent's application user can read and write the standard scheduling tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Assigning matching team roles grants the agent access to custom tables used by optimizations.
claims.quote: If your optimizations use custom tables ... assign the matching security roles to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team so that the agent can read and update those tables.

claims.claim: Team roles are assigned in Power Platform admin center through environment > Settings > Teams > Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, select your environment, and then go to Settings > Teams. ... Select the Scheduling Operations Agent Team. ... Assign the security roles that grant access to the tables your optimizations use

claims.claim: The team must be added to field security profiles for secured columns referenced by scopes or queries.
claims.quote: If you use column-level security (field security profiles) on any columns that your scopes or queries reference, also add the Scheduling Operations Agent Team to the matching field security profile.

claims.claim: Missing field security profile access can cause ignored filter conditions and incorrect results.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the agent might ignore filter conditions on those columns and return incorrect results.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Optimize booking statuses permit the agent to move or delete bookings.
claims.quote: Optimize: The agent can move or delete bookings with this status to generate an optimal schedule.

claims.claim: Unset booking optimization methods are treated as Do Not Move.
claims.quote: If you don't set this field, the agent treats all bookings in that status as Do Not Move.

claims.claim: Booking status Optimization Method offers Optimize, Do Not Move and Ignore.
claims.quote: For each booking status, set the Optimization Method property to one of the following values: ... Optimize ... Do Not Move ... Ignore

claims.claim: Do Not Move is suitable for work in progress or an arrival time committed to a customer.
claims.quote: This method typically applies when a technician is already traveling to a booking or has started or completed the work. You can also use this optimization method in situations where a specific arrival time was committed to a customer.

claims.claim: Apply method is at Resource Scheduling app > Settings > Optimization > Scheduling Plans > plan > Apply method.
claims.quote: In the Settings area of the Resource Scheduling app, under Optimization, select Scheduling Plans ... For Apply method, select Review before apply or Apply automatically.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A scope defines the resources, unfulfilled requirements and existing bookings a batch optimization considers.
claims.quote: A scope defines the set of data that a batch optimization operates over - which resources to optimize, which unfulfilled requirements to consider, and which existing bookings the agent can change.

claims.claim: A scope stores the fetchXML query, not a reference to the source view.
claims.quote: A scope stores the fetchXML query that's evaluated when the optimization runs, not a reference to the view used.

claims.claim: Scope query results exceeding optimization limits are truncated.
claims.quote: If a query returns more records than the optimization supports, the agent truncates the list.

claims.quote: A resource with a capacity greater than 1 counts as one resource for each capacity point.

claims.quote: Interactive optimizations ... Jobs (existing bookings and open requirements) | Up to 120.

claims.claim: Exceeding resource or job limits causes records to be dropped, or failure if existing bookings alone exceed the job limit.
claims.quote: When an optimization has more resources or jobs than the limit allows, the agent keeps the most relevant records and drops the rest. ... If the existing bookings alone exceed the jobs limit, the optimization fails.

claims.claim: With Always match time window selected, an expired promise window causes a booking in the optimization range to be deleted from the suggested schedule.
claims.quote: If you select this option and a booking in the optimization range has an expired promise window, the agent deletes that booking from the suggested schedule.

claims.quote: It doesn't support resources of type Equipment, Pool, and Facility. ... It doesn't support requirement groups or multiday requirements ... A resource can have up to three breaks per work day or shift. With four or more breaks, the agent returns an error.

claims.claim: Learn places the agent in Field Service's Azure regions except Azure Government and China.
